title: A stalk isomorphism spreads to a neighbourhood section
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $f:Y\to X$ be a locally finite-type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $y\in Y$ with $x=f(y)$. Suppose the induced local homomorphism $f^\sharp_y:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then there are an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq X$ of $x$ and a morphism $s:W\to Y$ with $f\circ s$ the inclusion of $W$, $s(x)=y$, and $s^\sharp_x=(f^\sharp_y)^{-1}$ under the canonical identification $\mathcal O_{W,x}=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Equivalently $s$ factors as a section $W\to f^{-1}(W)$ of the restricted morphism.

source.place: Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4), construction and spreading of the inverse local map; Morphisms Tag 0BX6 (lemma-morphism-defined-local-ring), case (2)(c).

proof.text: Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\alpha=f^\sharp_y$ and $\beta=\alpha^{-1}:B\to R$. The inverse is local: a ring isomorphism preserves units, hence the nonunits, which are the maximal ideal of a local ring. By the point-and-local-map bijection, $(y,\beta)$ determines $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}R\to Y$ sending the closed point $z$ to $y$. Let $c_x:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ be the canonical morphism, corresponding to $(x,\mathrm{id}_R)$. The composite $f\circ\varphi$ sends $z$ to $x$; its normalized stalk map is $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}_R$, by composition of stalk maps. Thus the injectivity of the same bijection gives $f\circ\varphi=c_x$.

source.place: Tag 01J6, lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring; Equation 02NA, equation-canonical-morphism; stalk composition: sheaves.tex Tag 008M, lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks.

proof.text: Apply the spreading lemma with $S=T=X$, $a=\mathrm{id}_X$, $Z=Y$, $g=f$, $t=x$, and the morphism $\varphi$ just constructed. Its hypotheses are exactly that $X$ is locally Noetherian, that $f$ is locally of finite type, and $f\circ\varphi=\mathrm{id}_X\circ c_x$. It yields an open neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ and $s:W\to Y$ satisfying $f\circ s=\iota_W$ and $s\circ c_{x,W}=\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 0BX6, lemma-morphism-defined-local-ring, (2)(c), applied as in varieties.tex Tag 0BFP, lemma-modification-normal-iso-over-codimension-1, proof (4).

proof.text: The canonical map $c_{x,W}$ sends the closed point to $x$, so evaluation of $s\circ c_{x,W}=\varphi$ there gives $s(x)=y$. Its normalized stalk map at that closed point is the identity under $\mathcal O_{W,x}=R$. Taking normalized stalk maps in the same equality therefore gives $s^\sharp_x=\beta$, using the composition formula. Finally $f\circ s=\iota_W$ says that the pair $(s,\mathrm{id}_W)$ gives a morphism to $Y\times_X W$, which is the open subscheme $f^{-1}(W)$ with its inclusion into $Y$ and the restriction of $f$ as projections [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], whose projection to $W$ is the identity. Conversely composing such a section with $f^{-1}(W)\to Y$ gives $s$ with the same identity. This proves the equivalent formulation.
